title: fix(worktrees): give chat writes breathing room during large cleanup
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A large retired-worktree deletion can keep generating filesystem metadata work for several minutes and delay chat transcript writes even below the 40 GiB reservation watermark added in #202563. One reported deletion lasted 392 seconds with a 6.34-second btrfs commit and multi-second foreground writer delays.

Related: #202197, #202563, #202204.

## User Impact

User impact: optional Linux cleanup yields sooner when filesystem commits slow down and splits large trees into shorter passes, giving foreground writers quiet intervals. Reclaiming a large tree takes longer by design. Retention, lossless removal and recovery snapshots are unchanged; no configuration or schema migration is required. This is a mitigation, not a guarantee of shared-filesystem transaction latency.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing pressure probe: removal reacts to an in-progress or newly observed btrfs commit taking at least 500 ms. Linux deletion yields at pressure or 30 seconds elapsed. The existing serialized deletion owner keeps the queue quiet for 30 seconds, then resumes unfinished files behind already queued siblings. Its pending-path protection spans cooldowns, so orphan GC cannot take over an active removal. Files left in the retired directory provide restart progress; there is no new cursor store or scan cache.

The 40/20 GiB reservation policy remains; resumed passes start below the low watermark. Historical completed commit samples do not repeatedly block a restarted pass. Non-Linux platforms retain ordinary batch pacing. A single filesystem call can overshoot the pass budget, and each child retains its separate 30-minute timeout. Sustained external pressure can postpone reclamation indefinitely; failed or interrupted cleanup retains the existing recovery path.

We use observed commit statistics and quiet intervals instead of forcing `syncfs` on the shared filesystem. A forced sync would itself join the shared transaction; apparent file bytes are not a reliable delayed-reference estimate.

Also remove the two unused spawn-test fixtures left by #202522, along with their unused imports. Existing active fixture behavior and tests remain.

## Evidence

The 600 ms commit regression fails on the base (pressure remains false), as does the bounded-pass regression (the entire tree is deleted instead of yielding). Candidate worker/probe/service-removal-safety tests pass: **34 tests**. The real service test proves pending-path protection through a yield/cooldown while the original checkout name can be restored. Existing GC tests pass (**29**), and all four consumers of the trimmed spawn fixture pass (**26**). The two unchanged Gateway pressure-probe consumers also pass (**60**).

`pnpm check:changed` was run. An authoring error removing the still-used logger import was corrected; its affected tests and core typecheck replay pass. Required core test type shards, scripts typecheck and targeted formatting passed. The full-tree unused-export check still reports the exact-parent main regression below; this is not relabeled green.

Codex autoreview of the complete local change against `9d151f83665822939144b00546bf52c1488e7223` is scoped-clean through P2. An earlier review was interrupted before any verdict when the fixture-import error was found. Pr-simplify retained one pressure owner and one serialized deletion owner; production growth is net +32 lines, while the unused fixture removal deletes 137 net test-support lines.

### Measurement acceptance rule, declared before the campaign

The committed workload is `scripts/perf/retired-worktree-unlink-measure.ts`. Use a synthetic node_modules-shaped tree with 62,000 files / 1,142,784,000 apparent bytes and a reflink sibling on a disposable btrfs loopback mount. Run A/A controls then five serial A/B pairs, with frozen baseline/candidate bundles, real timers and host load recorded. Report wall time, CPU, V8 allocation, maximum pass duration and sampled metadata reservation. A 20% CPU/allocation regression requires investigation; longer total elapsed time from deliberate 30-second quiet intervals is the requested tradeoff.

Separately bind fake sysfs counters only inside a disposable mount namespace: reservations below 40 GiB and one fresh 600 ms commit per 8,192 removals. Verify pressure terminates a pass before further unlinks and that all passes eventually complete. Accelerated timer wall times are diagnostic only. Reuse the prior reservation proof; do not claim this fixture reproduces production SQLite stalls or the reported six-second commit. No production data or service access.

### Completed measurements

Node 26.12.1 / Linux 7.2.12-orbstack / btrfs-progs 6.2, disposable 32 GiB sparse loop image. Each fresh tree has 62,000 files, 1,142,784,000 apparent bytes and 63,242 total entries, plus a reflink sibling. A/A controls followed by five serial A/B pairs; no owned compilation/tests/checks overlapped timed runs. n=5 p95 is the maximum, not a production-tail estimate.

| Metric | Baseline median (min–p95) | Candidate median (min–p95) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Wall, s | 53.989 (51.452–54.290) | 83.576 (82.526–84.308) |
| Longest pass, s | 53.989 (51.452–54.289) | 30.049 (30.022–30.075) |
| CPU, s | 2.797 (1.255–3.710) | 3.162 (2.071–3.874) |
| V8 allocated, MB | 217.034 (209.271–219.277) | 235.390 (226.041–244.275) |
| Sampled may_use peak, GiB | 0.266 (0.243–0.293) | 0.263 (0.231–0.278) |

All trees complete. Each baseline uses one pass; each candidate uses two, separated by one 30-second quiet interval. Median longest-pass reduction **44.3%**; total elapsed **+54.8%** is the requested reclamation-throughput tradeoff. Instrumented CPU **+13.1%**, allocation **+8.5%**. A/A wall 54.433/54.326 s, CPU 3.559/3.531 s, allocation 219.890/217.208 MB. Every sample, including the low-CPU second baseline, is retained in the lane report.

The driver imports frozen worker entrypoints per pass; subprocess startup is excluded. CPU/allocation include instrumentation. Its 20 ms reservation sampler runs through the quiet interval too, adding roughly 1,500 reads for that interval; no estimated cost was subtracted. Actual reservation peaks stay below 0.3 GiB, so this is not a reproduction of the production stall or high reservation incident.

The separate fake-sysfs trace holds reservation at 39.6 GiB and publishes a fresh 600 ms commit per 8,192 removals. Baseline removes 63,242 entries in one pass. Candidate yields seven times at exactly 8,192 entries, then removes the final 5,898 in its eighth pass. Both complete; scheduled waits **49.4 → 259.4 s**. Accelerated physical time **9.825 → 9.614 s** is diagnostic only. Fake files were bind-mounted solely over task-owned loop filesystem counters inside a disposable private mount namespace; no production filesystem or data was used.

Exact reviewed head: `414db65688667024817f5fc9fba9124af4656151`. Exact-head [CI run 44781791763](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44781791763) succeeded: **40 jobs passed, 29 skipped**, no reruns. [ClawSweeper revision 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202607#issuecomment-7045852978), reviewed 2026-11-20 17:26:29 UTC, has **zero findings and zero open checklist items** on this head. The earlier measurement request is addressed; production foreground writer latency remains unverified.


### Main regression requiring follow-up

On exact base `9d151f83665822939144b00546bf52c1488e7223`, the canonical dead-export checker reports `settingsParentRoute` in `ui/src/lib/settings-navigation.ts`. #202521 / `b7b72dc5b0ef9418bd5ee81cec721b775b5fc524` removed its last external caller from `settings-sidebar.tsx`; an internal call remains. This lane does not edit UI modules. The two #202522 unused fixtures also reproduced on this base and are fixed here. No suppression or expected-failure exception is added.
